clue.text: Setting out, and putting on the scales what keeps things steady.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: raising the anchor as a ship departs

definitions.text: putting on the scales what keeps things steady
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: weighing the heavy object that holds a ship in place

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the nautical phrase literally: to weigh something is to put it on scales, and an anchor keeps a ship steady.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors raise the anchor at departure, so the nautical phrase is an idiom for a voyage beginning.

clue.text: Are Boston creams only eaten in DC?

definitions.text: Are Boston creams only eaten in DC?

parts.note: Boston cream pie, a custard-filled sponge cake
suggests the dessert is renamed after the capital city, as it was in old cookbooks

explanation.definitionFit: Boston cream pie descends from an older custard cake that cookbooks called by the first president's name.

clue.text: What the guy who doesn't want to see you may holler!

definitions.text: What the guy who doesn't want to see you may holler!

parts.note: a person avoiding a visitor
the call shouted to the visitor, absurdly from inside the house

explanation.definitionFit: Shouting that one is absent from behind the door is the classic self-defeating brush-off.

clue.text: It's not legal to do it in the ring.

definitions.text: It's not legal to do it in the ring.

parts.note: a foul blow
the boxing ring, where punches below the waistband are banned

explanation.definitionFit: Boxing rules forbid punches beneath the waistband, and the idiom now means any unfair attack.

clue.text: A hen's confused Thomas, the English dramatist.

indicators.note: the letters of a hen's are jumbled up

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A muddled hen is mistaken for an Elizabethan playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Nashe was an Elizabethan pamphleteer and playwright, a contemporary of Marlowe.

clue.text: A sort of clause that intensifies the action!

definitions.text: A sort of clause that intensifies the action!

parts.note: a grammatical clause type
modifies the verb, the action word, as an adverb does

explanation.definitionFit: An adverbial clause works like an adverb, qualifying the verb and so sharpening the action.

clue.text: What you might consider such things as your light bills?

definitions.text: What you might consider such things as your light bills?

parts.note: a category of household costs
electricity bills, charges for flowing power

explanation.definitionFit: Ongoing household costs are regular outgoings, and the electricity bill pays for electrical flow.

clue.text: It's nothing, passing judgment and getting on the stump.

parts.note: O is the round shape of zero
rating, assessing or scolding

explanation.surface: A candidate with nothing to say still passes judgment on the campaign trail.
explanation.walkthrough: On the stump is American for out campaigning, giving speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: Campaign speeches were once made from tree stumps, so being on the stump means making political speeches.

clue.text: An event I crashed, drunk, at the onset of September's shades.

indicators.note: a gatecrasher wrecks the arrangement of these letters

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
blind drunk, so blind alone means drunk

indicators.note: takes only the first letter of September's

parts.note: the month's name, whose first letter is used

explanation.surface: A drunken gatecrasher arrives at a party as autumn begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Slatted window coverings that shut out sunlight are a type of shade.

clue.text: Makes sense at places where lawmakers meet.

indicators.note: to make something of letters is to form a new word from them, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A legislature finally seems to make sense in the places where it sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Senates are upper legislative chambers, the halls where elected lawmakers convene.

clue.text: Statistically random, with 5 having something to sing, and it's back in Paris, too!

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
an aria is a solo song in an opera

indicators.note: the word is turned into French and then read backwards

parts.note: the French for and is et

explanation.surface: A rambling sentence piling statistics, music and Paris together.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5 is not a cross-reference to 5 Down but the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics a variate is a random variable, a quantity whose values follow chance.

clue.text: Where the kid gets paddled, at the back of the parade.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a spanking lands on the child's backside

definitions.text: at the back of the parade
definitions.meaning: second meaning: last in the procession

explanation.walkthrough: The rear is both the buttocks and the tail end of a line.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means positioned behind, and colloquially the backside is where a spanking lands.

clue.text: The best people have a point, with what the advertisers claim is a bit tamed down.

parts.note: E is east, a point of the compass

parts.words: what the advertisers claim is a bit tamed down
parts.note: advertisers spell light as LITE for low-calorie or milder products

explanation.surface: Top people, it seems, have a point when ads promise something milder.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the select top group in a society, the cream regarded as superior.

clue.text: It's one way to get around Venice, with a short date in the turbulent lagoon.

definitions.text: It's one way to get around Venice

indicators.note: places the short date inside the stirred letters
rough, churning water stirs these letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: A tourist braves a choppy Venetian lagoon on a brief romantic outing.
explanation.definitionFit: The gondola is the traditional flat-bottomed rowing boat that carries passengers along Venetian canals.

clue.text: Describing the beverage–or the guy who drinks it too much?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: adjective for a drink containing spirits

definitions.text: the guy who drinks it too much
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a person addicted to drink

explanation.walkthrough: One word is both the adjective for strong drink and the noun for its addict.
explanation.definitionFit: An intoxicating drink is so described, and a person dependent on liquor is called by the same word.

clue.text: Incised carvings shown in a glint, I find.

indicators.note: the carvings are displayed in a new form made from these letters, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An engraved gem catches the light in a glint.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural is the Italian one, as with intaglio.
explanation.definitionFit: Intaglio work is design cut into a surface, so these are engraved, sunken carvings.

clue.text: Relating to a toothache, with some who don't, I can see.

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used, a run lying inside them

parts.note: the words whose inner run of letters gives the answer

explanation.surface: A dentist observes that some patients never suffer toothache.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans the apostrophe and comma.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means pertaining to teeth, from the Greek root found in orthodontist.

clue.text: Paddle with one in the water–usually in deep tropical waters.

parts.note: an oar is a paddle for rowing
a fish is a creature living in water

explanation.surface: A rower with a companion in the sea, out in deep tropical waters.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the creature by its habitat.
explanation.definitionFit: The oarfish is a very long ribbon-shaped species found at depth in warm oceans.

clue.text: The French unknown quantity and a final image provide a special reference.

parts.note: le is French for the
x is the algebraist's usual unknown
an icon is an image

explanation.surface: French algebra and a last picture combine into a reference work.
explanation.definitionFit: A lexicon is a dictionary, especially of a particular language or field, a specialised word book.

clue.text: That's where your brain comes in! It's rum I can handle, too!

definitions.text: That's where your brain comes in!

indicators.note: to handle letters is to manipulate them into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A drinker boasts of brains while claiming they can handle rum.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum looks like an oddness signal but is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull encloses the brain, so the brain sits inside it.

clue.text: Analyze a word with spare parts.

indicators.note: the word spare is split into parts and rebuilt, so its letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Studying a word as though it were assembled from spare parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare parts' reads as one phrase, but the second word is the signal acting on the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To parse is to break a word or sentence down grammatically, a schoolroom form of analysis.

clue.text: A type of fern might be the last thing you see going over the fence!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a primitive rush-like plant related to ferns

definitions.text: might be the last thing you see going over the fence
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: a jumping steed's rear end disappearing

explanation.walkthrough: The second half pictures a horse clearing a fence, its tail the last part in view.
explanation.definitionFit: Equisetum, the plant called by this name, is a fern ally, while a horse's tail trails a leaping mount.

clue.text: Going up and down, the way a sort of umpire starts to cite something?

indicators.note: reads the same going up or down the grid, so it is a palindrome
only the start of the official's title is used, the end dropped

parts.note: a referee is an umpire in many sports

explanation.surface: An umpire citing something as he paces up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: The official's title is cut short to its start, and the shortened word reads the same either way down the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer to a source is to mention or quote it as an authority, much like citing.

clue.text: Living near the surface of the ground in the wrong age, with a sort of pile around it.

definitions.text: Living near the surface of the ground

indicators.note: the rearranged pile letters go round the other group
only a kind of pile, so its letters come out rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the letters of age put in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A naturalist describes shallow-dwelling creatures in a pile of earth from the wrong era.
explanation.definitionFit: Epigeal organisms or plant parts grow or live at or just above the soil, a botanical and zoological term.

clue.text: Make things according to the custom.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to shape or craft, used as a verb
second meaning: a prevailing manner or way of doing things

explanation.walkthrough: One word serves as a verb for crafting and as a noun for the usual way of doing things.
explanation.definitionFit: To fashion is to form or construct, and a fashion is a manner or customary practice.

clue.text: What was the crooner dreaming of!

definitions.text: What was the crooner dreaming of!

parts.note: Bing Crosby, the crooner who made the Irving Berlin song famous
quotes the song's opening line, a snowy holiday the singer longs for

explanation.definitionFit: Crosby's best-selling record opens with the singer dreaming of a snowy Yuletide.
